protocol.scope_summary: SUPPORTING DOCUMENT (not a prescribing protocol). This is the 'Summary of updates: 7 April 2026' change log for the Queensland Community Pharmacy Chronic Conditions Management Pilot clinical protocols, produced as part of a routine review concluded in March 2026. It states it 'is not an exhaustive list of all updates made to the Pilot clinical protocols'. It contains no eligibility criteria, diagnosis pathways, treatments, red flags or follow-up rules of its own: every clinical statement in it describes changes to OTHER protocols (Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program, COPD Monitoring Program, CVD Risk Reduction Program - hypertension / blood glucose / lipid modification) and is recorded in open_questions with page provenance rather than as criteria of a protocol.

references: The updated clinical protocols can be located here (link text as printed; target URL not present in the extracted text) (page 1)
Australian Asthma Handbook (named as the source for updated eligibility and pharmacotherapy guidance) (page 1)
National Asthma Council Australia Spirometry Handbook for Primary Care (added as a resource) (page 3)
Lung Foundation resource on inhaler technique (added) (page 5)

open_questions.topic: General updates across all clinical protocols (changes, not this document's criteria)
open_questions.observed: Section 'General updates across all clinical protocols' records: Referral and Eligibility criteria combined into an Eligibility section; criteria updated 'in line with contemporary guidance, including updates to the Australian Asthma Handbook'; a new 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' section added to identify patient criteria requiring concurrent referral with treatment; clarification of patients appropriate for enrolment and entry points (Overview of the Program); Figure 1 updated; pharmacotherapy advice clarified that 'combination products that only include medicines able to be prescribed under the Program can be prescribed, if indicated'; link to editable Lifestyle prescription and CVD Risk Management Plan added; appendices updated.
open_questions.why_unclear: These are changes applied to the underlying protocols across all pages of the affected protocols; the resulting criteria live in those protocols, not here.

open_questions.topic: Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program - eligibility changes
open_questions.observed: Protocol 'updated significantly to align with contemporary management and the updated Australian Asthma Handbook'. Ineligibility criteria extended to include: patients experiencing respiratory distress; chest tightness or discomfort during/after exercise (without other symptoms of asthma); clinical features or symptoms suggestive of a respiratory condition other than asthma not suitable for management under the Program; patients currently receiving specialist care without a written referral from specialist or general practitioner; history of anaphylaxis; alarm signs and symptoms; history of severe asthma exacerbation/s; poor asthma symptom control despite Level 3 pharmacotherapy requiring treatment consistent with Level 4 pharmacotherapy; current/equivalent Level 4 pharmacotherapy; previous diagnosis of severe asthma or restrictive lung disease; FEV1 <60% predicted; history of moderate or severe COPD; type 1 diabetes; poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; heart failure, pulmonary hypertension or Cor pulmonale; suspected or confirmed food allergy; history of sudden-onset acute asthma. Previously embedded criteria moved into Eligibility (remain ineligible): contraindications to spirometry (that will not resolve with time) without an existing diagnosis of asthma; spirometry results that are difficult to interpret/unexpected for asthma or indicate alarm symptoms or findings. Criteria REMOVED (now eligible): patients who have chronic kidney disease; patients with mild COPD. Terminology changes: 'mild to moderate asthma' terminology removed; rapid-acting bronchodilators (rather than relievers) and inhaled corticosteroid-containing medicines (ICS; rather than preventers).
open_questions.why_unclear: These are eligibility changes to the Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program clinical protocol; the operative criterion wording and combinatorics must be read from that protocol, which is not this document.

open_questions.topic: Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program - treat-and-refer and assessment changes
open_questions.observed: 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' criteria revised/new (eligible but must be concurrently referred): symptoms and features that favour both asthma and mild COPD where there is no diagnosis of co-existing mild COPD; suspected respiratory bacterial infection that requires antibiotic therapy; well controlled type 2 diabetes; requiring ≥12 short-acting beta2 agonist (SABA) canisters in a year; suspected or confirmed aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease. Also: additional/expanded patient history considerations for Asthma case taking; updated management of features of both mild COPD and asthma; updated physical examination guidance; updated guidance on when spirometry is recommended (recently diagnosed patients with prior spirometry need not repeat it to establish baseline); recommendation to manage the patient under the Program until spirometry can be undertaken if community-pharmacy spirometry cannot be conducted and external access is delayed; National Asthma Council Australia Spirometry Handbook for Primary Care added; symptom control assessment guidance updated; non-pharmacological measures updated (self-monitoring, allergen avoidance, thunderstorm asthma, immunisation).
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying asthma protocol, recorded here with page provenance rather than as this document's criteria.

open_questions.topic: Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program - pharmacotherapy and review changes (includes a practitioner restriction)
open_questions.observed: Pharmacotherapy guidance updated: consider the current Australian Asthma Handbook in conjunction with Therapeutic Guidelines, and 'if the Australian Asthma Handbook and Therapeutic Guidelines differ, to refer to the Australian Asthma Handbook when making clinical decisions'; ICS indicated for all adults and adolescents with asthma and 'should never be withdrawn completely/deprescribed'; new recommended treatment levels with a 'recommended' and 'alternative' option for each level; short-acting beta2 agonists not appropriate to be used alone as-needed without concomitant ICS; 'montelukast no longer having a role in the routine management of asthma in adolescents and adults, and that a pharmacist must not initiate treatment under the Program'; management considerations for co-existing asthma and COPD; updated step up/step down/switching guidance; updated management of asthma exacerbations and acute asthma including circumstances where patients require oral corticosteroids and the quantity to be prescribed; management of patients entering with an existing medicine regimen. Clinical review: 'Revised clinical review timeframes'; requirement added for monitoring and review of conditions that impact on asthma control/management (Appendix 2).
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying asthma protocol; the new treatment levels, timeframes and quantities are not printed in this summary.

open_questions.topic: COPD Monitoring Program - eligibility and treat-and-refer changes
open_questions.observed: New guidance: manage patients with symptoms/features of mild COPD and asthma (including co-existing diagnoses) who are eligible for the COPD Monitoring Program under the Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program clinical protocol. Ineligibility criteria extended to include: respiratory distress; chest tightness or discomfort (without other symptoms of COPD); suspected respiratory condition other than COPD not suitable for management; patients receiving specialist care without written referral; new/poorly controlled mental health condition; FEV1 <60% predicted; history of moderate and severe COPD; complex cardiovascular disease; vascular or cerebrovascular conditions; alarm signs/symptoms; type 1 diabetes or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; worsening of COPD symptoms despite adequate management or at Step 3 pharmacotherapy and requiring treatment consistent with triple inhaler therapy. Previously embedded criteria moved into Eligibility (remain ineligible): contraindications to spirometry (that will not resolve with time); spirometry results difficult to interpret/unexpected for COPD or indicating alarm symptoms or findings. Criteria REMOVED (now eligible): patients with asthma*; patients with symptoms and features that favour both asthma and mild COPD*. Treat-and-refer (eligible but concurrently referred): well controlled type 2 diabetes; stable/well controlled mental health condition; signs and symptoms of cognitive impairment or diagnosis of dementia or another neurocognitive condition; suspected bacterial infection that requires antibiotic therapy; patients aged <45 years not investigated for alpha1-antitrypsin deficiency.
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying COPD Monitoring Program protocol; operative wording and combinatorics must be read from that protocol.

open_questions.topic: COPD Monitoring Program - assessment, testing and pharmacotherapy changes
open_questions.observed: Overview of the Program: pulmonary rehabilitation and lung cancer screening added as interventions that may be recommended. Figure 1: Piko-6 screening device removed as no longer available in Australia; revised timeframe for contraindications to initial testing with a COPD screening device. Targeted case finding: screening device use is for screening purposes only and does not replace spirometry to determine diagnosis. Program eligibility: recommendation to encourage smoking cessation even if the patient is ineligible. Patient history: expanded COPD case-taking considerations, clarity on bronchodilator use, updated symptoms of stable COPD (Table 1), updated management of features of both mild COPD and asthma (manage under Improved Asthma Symptom Control Program if eligible for COPD Monitoring Program). Assess COPD severity: impact of symptoms added; timing of severity assessment added; CAT renamed Chronic Airways Assessment Test (CAAT); mMRC Dyspnoea Scale added. Conduct spirometry: recency requirement changed 'from within the previous 3 months to within the previous 12 months'. Management plan: AMH removed as a primary resource for COPD Action Plan and Lifestyle prescription; new subsection 'COPD action plan and lifestyle prescription'. Non-pharmacological: vaccination recommendations updated; lung cancer screening referral added for eligible patients. Pharmacotherapy: existing-regimen guidance updated; inhaler considerations updated with Lung Foundation inhaler technique resource; resource added to assess COPD exacerbation severity; updated self-management of mild and moderate COPD exacerbations including circumstances requiring oral corticosteroids and the quantity to be prescribed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying COPD protocol; new timeframes and quantities are not printed here.

open_questions.topic: CVD Risk Reduction Program - hypertension protocol eligibility and treatment changes (numeric thresholds appear only as change notes)
open_questions.observed: Ineligibility extended to include: patients receiving specialist care without written referral; retinopathy, neuropathy or nephropathy; poorly controlled asthma, moderate or severe COPD, severe OSA or another serious respiratory illness; current deep vein thrombosis; current pulmonary embolism or history of pulmonary embolism; suspected hypertension with a secondary cause; total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥5.0 mmol/L or triglycerides ≥6 mmol/L; severe hyperglycaemia or blood glucose level ≥20.0 mmol/L, or hypoglycaemia; inability to reach (and stabilise) blood pressure clinical target after 4-6 weeks of treatment with 2 first line antihypertensives at maximum tolerated doses. Criteria REMOVED (now eligible): well controlled asthma; mild COPD. Treat-and-refer: type 2 diabetes managed with insulin; history of deep vein thrombosis but not currently on any antithrombotic therapy. Other changes: type 2 diabetes risk assessment recommendations updated; CVD risk assessment recommendations updated (moderate to severe CKD or familial hypercholesteremia predetermined at high CVD risk with no calculation needed; for patients already on pharmacological therapy or previously assessed high-risk, review individual risk factors - formal reassessment not recommended); 'who and when' recommended tests carried out updated (Table 1); 'Updated blood pressure cutoff for pharmacotherapy recommendations in patients ≥45 years (≥30 years for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people) with intermediate CVD risk'; Appendix 1 cholesterol reference levels in Table 7 updated; normal uACR recommendation updated.
open_questions.why_unclear: These numeric thresholds are recorded as changes to the underlying CVD hypertension protocol; they are not criteria of this document, and the printed summary does not state the actual cutoff values, which must be read from that protocol.

open_questions.topic: CVD Risk Reduction Program - blood glucose protocol changes
open_questions.observed: Ineligibility extended to include: patients receiving specialist care without written referral; retinopathy, neuropathy or nephropathy; poorly controlled asthma, moderate or severe COPD, severe OSA or another serious respiratory illness; current deep vein thrombosis; current pulmonary embolism or history of pulmonary embolism; total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥5.0 mmol/L or triglycerides ≥6 mmol/L; inability to reach clinical targets within appropriate timeframe despite 2 antihyperglycemic medicines at optimal dose. Criteria REMOVED (now eligible): well controlled asthma; mild COPD. Treat-and-refer (new criterion): history of deep vein thrombosis but not currently on any antithrombotic therapy. Monitoring and clinical targets: serum B12 testing recommendation added for patients taking metformin (Table 2); HbA1c review timeframe recommendations (Table 3) updated with different recommendations for newly diagnosed patients or those undergoing therapeutic changes. Patient self-management: 'Reminder added to advise patients to withhold metformin or GLP-1 receptor agonist if they have vomiting, diarrhoea, or are not eating much.' Clinical review and ongoing collaboration: revised clinical review timeframes.
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying blood glucose protocol; review timeframes and target values are not printed in this summary.

open_questions.topic: CVD Risk Reduction Program - lipid modification protocol changes
open_questions.observed: Ineligibility extended to include: patients receiving specialist care without written referral; retinopathy, neuropathy or nephropathy; poorly controlled asthma, moderate or severe COPD, severe OSA or another serious respiratory illness; current deep vein thrombosis; current pulmonary embolism or history of pulmonary embolism; severe hyperglycaemia or blood glucose level ≥20.0 mmol/L), or hypoglycaemia; abnormal lipid profile (but not severely elevated levels) where CVD risk cannot be determined because the risk calculator is not validated for their population (e.g. 18-29 years old); dyslipidaemia with a secondary cause; unable to reach lipid levels clinical targets after 6 months of lipid modifying therapy. Criteria REMOVED (now eligible): well controlled asthma; mild COPD. Treat-and-refer: type 2 diabetes managed with insulin; history of deep vein thrombosis but not currently on any antithrombotic therapy. Pharmacotherapy approach to lipid modification consolidated into Table 1. Referral recommendation added for patients with abnormal lipid levels (but not severe hyperlipidaemia) who cannot have their CVD risk calculated.
open_questions.why_unclear: Changes to the underlying lipid modification protocol; the actual criteria wording, Table 1 content and referral destination are not printed here.
